_note: Big-picture campaign design doc for the Session 0 reboot. NOT a live entity — not referenced in index.json, not loaded by the app. Working reference only until we break it down into actual entities/sessions.
title: The Veil of Thanatos
status: draft — big picture only, not yet broken into entities or sessions

premise.the_veil: F.A.I.L. Academy sits atop a thin veil separating the Material Plane from Thanatos, the 333rd layer of the Abyss, ruled by the demon prince Orcus.
premise.founding_purpose: The founders discovered the veil and built the Academy at this location specifically to maintain control over the weak point, for defensive purposes.
premise.incidents: Occasionally something leaks through the veil, causing localized 'incidents' at the Academy. For most of the Academy's history this has been rare and manageable.
premise.founders_departure: When the founders departed the Academy (each by different means), they did not pass along their knowledge of the veil. They believed the glyphs, wards, and other magical defenses they left behind would be sufficient on their own.
premise.current_problem: That confidence was partly misplaced. The veil has lately been stretching wider with each passing year, and the wards are no longer holding it as tightly as they once did.

antagonist.identity: Corvin Ashworth (he/him) — an unremarkable scholarship student at the Academy, easy to overlook, which is exactly why Torvald Thatch's attention meant something to him. Graduated roughly 6 years before campaign start. See phase2_the_one_who_got_away.json and torvald_the_insider.json for full depth.
antagonist.possession: At some point they were possessed by something originating from Thanatos.
antagonist.goal: They left the Academy intending to grow their power enough to tear the veil open wide.
antagonist.thornwick_connection: They first encountered the Thornwick Arcane Consortium during a student expedition (which one is not yet specified — placeholder). After graduating, they approached Thornwick directly with the intent to subvert their former school by any means necessary.
antagonist.operation: They are the one responsible for the corrupting magical items being planted around campus (see phase1_something_is_happening.json's three incidents) — delivered via an unidentified 'inside person' on campus. See phase2_the_one_who_got_away.json for the insider brainstorm; not yet decided.
antagonist.status: At large; current whereabouts unknown to the party at campaign start.
antagonist.phase_boundary_note: Per instruction, none of this antagonist material appears in Phase 1 — the party doesn't learn about the former student until Phase 2. Phase 1 clues only establish that incidents are happening and that the veil exists.

core_plot: The players must discover what is happening to the veil and why, track down the possessed former student, and stop them before they gain enough power to return and tear the veil open.

party.session_zero_reboot: Sessions 1-5 PCs are retired/archived canon. The active party is entirely new: fifth-year students in their final year, about to graduate.
party.relationship_to_npcs: As long-tenured students, they know the Academy's faculty and staff well — years of personal history, not stranger introductions. This applies especially to figures like Ellery Voss, Headmistress Dowe, and Torvald Thatch, and matters mechanically: they know these people's normal demeanor well enough to clock a deviation from it.
party.relationship_to_the_mystery: They have no personal investigative history with the incidents — everything they know going in is third-party campus rumor, same as any other student. Their engagement should start curiosity-driven, not procedural: noticing something feels off about people they already know and care about, rather than building a case like outside investigators. Hooks and clues across all phases should be written with this in mind.

phases.name: Something is Happening
phases.goal: The party learns that incidents at the Academy are escalating and begins to uncover why — the existence of the veil, its history, and its current instability.

phases.name: The One Who Got Away
phases.goal: The party learns about the possessed former student and locates them.

phases.name: Closing the Veil
phases.goal: The party stops the former student from gaining enough power to return and rip the veil open.

continuity_notes.prior_lore: Some lore from sessions 1-5 is being retained (the veil/founders concept is built on top of existing Academy history). Which specific prior threads/entities (e.g. the Secret Society, the Ninth Thesis, Occult Systems, the founders' individual dm-only lore) map onto this new picture is not yet decided — TBD in a later pass.

founders_persona_rewrite.decision: The same three founders already in the data (Aldric Voss, Isolde Orath, Brennan Ashcroft) are being kept as-is in identity, but their personas and relationships are being rewritten to fit the new plot: they were genuinely good people who believed that founding the Academy — concentrating a high density of powerful heroes, faculty, and students in one place — was the right way to build a defense against the veil and a potential evil incursion.
founders_persona_rewrite.consequence: Any existing lore about the founders (or things tied closely to them, e.g. the Secret Society, the Ninth Thesis, Occult Systems) that conflicts with this well-intentioned framing needs to be rewritten. CATALOGUED (2026-07-27) — see founders_persona_audit.json for the full conflict list, resolution options, and the verified backlink migration list. The core issue: live brennan_ashcroft.html/secret_society.html say Ashcroft founded it as a mundane 'Alumni Society,' while the reboot's confirmed the_ninth_thesis.json says Aldric Voss founded it around Wren Halloway's thesis — a direct contradiction, not yet resolved. occult_systems.html's ritual/sacrifice material also has no proposed home in the rewrite. Both need a DM decision before the merge is executed.

continuity_notes.the_ninth_thesis: See the_ninth_thesis.json — Voss runs the Ninth Thesis, an organization hunting hidden evil in the world, now investigating the campus incidents. CONFIRMED: it IS the existing secret_society entity (to be merged into ninth_thesis); CONFIRMED: founded by Aldric Voss ~350 years ago around student Wren Halloway's suppressed graduation thesis, led by successive Voss descendants since. Merge not yet executed against live data.
continuity_notes.veil_origin: See the_dwarven_ruins.json — CONFIRMED: the veil's presence at this location traces back to an ancient dwarven city (now ruins, near the edge of campus) that ruptured the barrier to Thanatos through means TBD. The founders discovered the already-existing veil generations later; they did not cause it. Ruins are a late-game location — the party should not visit them in Phase 1/early Phase 2. A bulette displaced from near the ruins gives Phase 1 its first non-sabotage incident, and fills the montage gap in session1_something_is_happening.json.
continuity_notes.sessions_6_9: Removed per prior instruction; this arc supersedes them.
continuity_notes.retired_party_roster_correction: CORRECTED (2026-07-23): 'Ozzy' was never a fifth party member — it's the DM's own nickname for [[oswald_crumb|Professor Oswald Crumb]] (both goblins). The 'Ozzy' file is a legitimate DM-built combat stat block for Crumb (Sorcerer 10, built so he could be run accurately in the Session 5 Nether Mountains ambush) — it was just mis-modeled as a standalone 'Player Character' npc entity instead of being linked to Crumb. Fixed: re-id'd to oswald_crumb_statblock (visibility dm-only, category Faculty, content moved to content/npcs/), cross-linked both directions with oswald_crumb.html. The retired Sessions 1-5 PLAYER party is four members: Lugeiros Serise, Gunnar, Caelum Rivenstone, BloodRaven — Crumb was an NPC they hired, not one of them.
continuity_notes.retired_party_timeline: CONFIRMED (2026-07-23, from Session 0 relationship-table notes): the retired Sessions 1-5 party (Lugeiros Serise, Gunnar, Caelum Rivenstone, BloodRaven) are NOT graduated or gone — their one-shots share the same campus timeline as the new party's tenure, and they are current UNDERCLASSMEN relative to the new (fifth-year, about-to-graduate) party. 'Retired' means retired from play, not retired from the setting. They're fair game as recurring NPCs going forward — see guntrah.html's relationship with [[lugeiros_serise|Lugeiros Serise]] for the first concrete instance of this (the Cover Story bond, Session 0).
